Hello, and thank you! Also in the same boat (R 3.1.0, under Mac 10.9.2, with GTK_2.24.17-X11.pkg <http://r.research.att.com/libs/GTK_2.24.17-X11.pkg> installed from http://r.research.att.com/ , and install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com", type="source”)  ).

I got the same problem; from source also did not quite work:

> install.packages("RGtk2", type="source")

trying URL 'http://cran.stat.ucla.edu/src/contrib/RGtk2_2.20.29.tar.gz'
Content type 'application/x-tar' length 2785355 bytes (2.7 Mb)
opened URL
==================================================
downloaded 2.7 Mb

* installing *source* package ‘RGtk2’ ...
** package ‘RGtk2’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
checking for pkg-config... no
checking for INTROSPECTION... no
checking for GTK... no
configure: error: GTK version 2.8.0 required
ERROR: configuration failed for package ‘RGtk2’
* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.1/Resources/library/RGtk2’

The downloaded source packages are in
    ‘/private/var/folders/gv/dsf22lls2yj8tzwcgnp4yr7w0000gn/T/RtmpQLoLph/downloaded_packages’
Warning message:
In install.packages("RGtk2", type = "source") :
  installation of package ‘RGtk2’ had non-zero exit status
>

The GTK installer did produce /Library/Frameworks/GTK+.framework but apparently R doesn't see it... Is there just something I need to do to let R know the GTK framework is there?

(Or is it necessary to install GTK by using macports as described on the GitHub link, instead?)

Thanks again,
Linda

messages.body_plain:
Jessica and Steven,

For what it's worth: I was getting the same error as you, but just got Rattle working for the first time, by changing these steps:
1. Using the R-3.1.0-snowleopard.pkg <http://cran.cnr.berkeley.edu/bin/macosx/R-3.1.0-snowleopard.pkg> from CRAN and not the R-3.1.0-mavericks.pkg <http://cran.cnr.berkeley.edu/bin/macosx/R-3.1.0-mavericks.pkg> (even though I am running Mavericks X 10.9.3)
2. Installing and running everything through RStudio's interface to R: http://www.rstudio.com/

I did also use:

install.packages("RGtk2", type="source")

install.packages("rattle", repos="http://rattle.togaware.com", type="source")

Thanks and good luck,
LP

On Saturday, February 16, 2013 11:42:11 PM UTC-5, Graham Williams wrote:

I've probably not got all the possible combinations for all of the types of databases working correctly in Rattle for every case yet.

As a work-around, copy the command out of the log and paste it into the console, then add the schema and save the result into "ds" for example (rather than crs$dataset). Then choose to load ds as an R Dataset into Rattle.

messages.subject: Feature-Request: Multi-Class classifier (one-vs-all) in Rattle ... ??
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have observed that I can't use NN model in case my classes variable has more than 2 values .... and same I cannot use logistic regression on the same data ... and others ..

.. my quick assessment is that those prediction algorithms (in the form of the provided algorithms in R which are utilized by Rattle) can be used as binary classifiers  only ...

.. that brought me to the idea that if there would be an implementation of a generic "one-vs-all" classifier -> then we can plug logistic regression / NN and others and analyze multi-class data ....

.. all that could be considered in conjunction with my proposal to provide "scheduler" for training/scoring (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rattle-users/uu5iEDX_5y0)

.. having such scheduler -> you can schedule training of multiple classifiers and then use one-vs-all scoring on trained models to evaluate your prediction ...

That would be cool or ? :) I know its probably not that easy as it sounds written here :)

ric.
